refuted.claim: Fact #21 (marked "verified"): "1410 load-mode card input sets word marks but never clears them... This is a real divergence from 1401 load-mode behaviour and the implementer must not copy the 1401 rule."
refuted.why: Two separate errors. (1) The 'never clears them' half is not in the source. A22-0526-3 p.41 states only what a word separator DOES ('A single word separator in incoming data is stored in core storage as a word mark over the next incoming character'); it says nothing about positions NOT preceded by a separator. An absent statement is not a verified negative, so the confidence tag is wrong. The only 1410 emulator implementation available does the opposite: SIMH i7010_chan.c line 610 gates word-mark preservation on move mode only -- `if ((cmd[chan] & CHAN_LOAD) == 0) ch |= M[caddr[chan]] & WM;` -- so in load mode the stored character carries ONLY the separator-derived word-mark bit and any pre-existing word mark in that position is destroyed. (2) The 1401 comparison is backwards: there is no 1401 rule that clears word marks on card input to diverge from. IBM 1401 A24-1403-5, Read a Card: 'Word Marks. Word marks are undisturbed.' Read and Branch: 'Word marks are not affected.' Read Tape with Word Marks behaves exactly like 1410 load mode ('A word-separator character read from tape causes a word mark to be associated with the next tape character transferred to 1401 core storage'). The 1401 LOAD KEY sets a word mark at location 001 only, and the manual tells the programmer to clear storage first ('Before any program is loaded, all positions of storage should be cleared of data and word marks').
refuted.correction: Correct statement: A22-0526-3 p.41 documents only that a word separator SETS a word mark over the next character in load mode; it is silent on unmarked positions. The 1410 reference emulator (SIMH) models load mode as fully determining the word-mark bit from the separator stream, i.e. clearing pre-existing word marks over the loaded extent, and models move mode as preserving them. The 1401 does not clear word marks on card read either, so there is no 1401-vs-1410 divergence here and no 1401 rule to avoid copying. Drop the divergence warning entirely.
refuted.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3 p.41 (Move Mode / Load Mode) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf ; IBM 1401 Data Processing System Reference Manual A24-1403-5, Read a Card (p.44) and Variable Word Length / load key (p.35) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1401/A24-1403-5_1401_Reference_Apr62.pdf ; SIMH I7000 simulator i7010_chan.c (Richard Cornwell, 2005-2016), chan_write/word-mark logic ~lines 600-615 - https://github.com/open-simh/simh/blob/master/I7000/i7010_chan.c

refuted.claim: Fact #22 (marked "likely"): "DC and DS leave any pre-existing word mark in the target positions untouched, because (a) neither manual says the assembler emits a clear, and (b) the condensed-card / load-mode format has no encoding for 'clear the word mark here'. Only an explicit CW / CS instruction or an OS-Autocoder DA clear can remove one."
refuted.why: Premise (b) is false, and the closing sentence is false. (b): in load mode the word-mark bit of every stored character is determined by whether a word separator preceded it -- 'no separator' IS the encoding for 'no word mark here'. That is precisely how SIMH implements it (i7010_chan.c: preservation of `M[caddr] & WM` is applied only when CHAN_LOAD is clear). Since a DC emits real data characters into the condensed card (verified: C28-0309-1 p.13, 'the same characteristics as the dcw statement... the processor does not cause a word mark to be set'), those characters are loaded in load mode with no preceding separator, which under that model clears the word mark over the DC's own extent. Closing sentence: A22-0526-3 p.7 rule 2 itself allows word marks to be altered 'by a data move operation that specifies that they should be altered', and A22-0526-3 documents such an operation -- Move Characters and Suppress Zeros: 'B-field word marks within this specified area, including the leftmost position, are removed during the operation.' So CW/CS/clear-storage/DA-clear are not the only ways a word mark disappears. The DS half of the claim is sound and unaffected: DS emits nothing at all, so it cannot disturb anything.
refuted.correction: Split the claim. DS: correct as written -- nothing is punched, nothing is loaded, the area keeps whatever data and word marks were in core (C28-0326-2 p.30, verbatim: 'No information is entered into the area, no word mark is assigned by the processor, and the area is not cleared prior to reservation'). DC: unsafe as written -- a DC overwrites the data in its own positions and, under load-mode semantics as implemented by SIMH, also clears the word marks over those positions; only positions OUTSIDE any emitted card's extent are guaranteed untouched. Also drop 'only an explicit CW/CS instruction or an OS-Autocoder DA clear can remove one' -- a data move that alters word marks (e.g. Move Characters and Suppress Zeros) removes B-field word marks.
refuted.source: C28-0309-1 p.13 (DC) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf ; A22-0526-3 p.7 rule 2 and Move Characters and Suppress Zeros word-mark note - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf ; SIMH I7000 i7010_chan.c ~lines 600-615 - https://github.com/open-simh/simh/blob/master/I7000/i7010_chan.c

refuted.claim: Condensed-card table row: "| 70-72 | Relocation indicators if required (ignored by the Load Program) |"
refuted.why: Misattribution caused by OCR line-order. I read the actual Figure 2 page image (C28-0309-1 PDF page 7 = printed page 7). The figure's left rule marks column 72 for one CONTENTS entry and columns 73-80 for the next. The 72/71/70 entry reads only 'Relocation indicators (if required) occupy Cols 72, 71, 70....'. The sentence 'These columns are ignored by the Load Program and may contain any information desired by the user' is the entry for columns 73-80, and is immediately followed in that same entry by 'NOTE: Autocoder Processor places a card sequence number in Columns 73-75, and the program "Identification," if any, in Columns 76-80.' Logically too: relocation indicators exist to be consumed by a relocating loader, not ignored by it.
refuted.correction: Cols 70-72: relocation indicators (if required). Cols 73-80: ignored by the Load Program, may contain anything the user wants; the Autocoder processor puts the card sequence number in 73-75 and the program identification in 76-80.
refuted.source: IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1, p.7, Figure 2 'Condensed Card Format' (read as page image; the archive.org OCR text scrambles the figure's row order) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: MISSED AND MATERIAL: the low-order default applies to SYMBOLIC labels only. C28-0309-1 p.12, in the same DCW paragraph the finding quotes, continues: 'If a symbolic label is indented one position, the address of the high-order position of the constant will be assigned to the symbol. Actual labels always refer to the high-order position of the defined constant.' So a DCW/DC carrying an ACTUAL (absolute numeric) label resolves to the HIGH-order position with no indent, the inverse of the symbolic default. The finding quotes the indent sentence and stops one sentence short.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1, p.12 (DCW - Define Constant with Word Mark) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: Corroborating general rule for the above: 'Symbolic labels are written left-justified in the label field except as described in "dc" or "dcw." Actual labels are always written left-justified in the label field. This actual address refers to the high-order position of the instruction, constant, or defined field. Actual labels have no effect on the address assignment counters.' Note the last sentence -- an actual label does not advance or reset the location counter.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1, 'The Coding Sheet' / label-field description, printed pp.5-6 - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: MISSED: the condensed card's columns 8, 9 and 10 hold ZEROS. Figure 2's CARD COLUMN rule reads: col 1 = word separator (0-5-8); cols 2-6 = xxxxx high-order position of the area to load; col 7 = word separator; cols 8-10 = 0 0 0; cols 11-12 = xx number of characters to load; col 13 onward = instructions/data. The finding's condensed-card table jumps from col 7 to cols 11-12 and omits 8-10 entirely, which will misalign a byte-exact card-loader implementation.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1, p.7, Figure 2 (read as page image) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: MISSED, and an easy assembler bug: the asterisk operand has two different meanings. 'If an asterisk (*) appears as an operand in the source program, the processor will replace it with the actual core-storage address of the last character of the instruction in which it appears (except in equ, org, or ltorg statements, where the asterisk refers to the current position of the processor address assignment counter).' The finding's Appendix C row 'EOF EQU * -> 00216 = 00209+7' only works because EQU takes the counter meaning; in an ordinary operand the same * on that instruction would be 00215.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1, p.8 ('Asterisk (*)' under Address Types) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: Independent object-deck proof of the low-order/high-order split that is stronger than the finding's ADDRS-column argument, because it uses the punched cards rather than the listing's address column. In the C28-0326-2 Appendix C object deck, one card has cols 2-6 = 00396 and count = 00012, so it loads 00396-00407; the two column-7-indented DC statements listed at ADDRS 00396 (CT 6) and 00402 (CT 6) therefore start at those addresses -- ADDRS is the HIGH-order position for them. A second card has cols 2-6 = 00204 and count = 00036, loading 00204-00239; the last constant on it, DCW EOJ (CT 5), is listed at ADDRS 00239, i.e. the final byte of the card -- ADDRS is the LOW-order position for a non-indented constant.
additions.source: IBM 1410/7010 OS Autocoder C28-0326-2, Appendix C, object-deck listing and assembly listing pp.56-57 - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0326-2_1410_OS_Autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: Partial answer to the finding's open question 1 (does the loader clear storage?). C28-0309-1 documents no clear, but it does document loader control flow that an emulator needs: an EX statement 'assembles a branch instruction... This instruction does not become part of the assembled machine-language program, but it causes the processor-produced loading routine to halt the loading process at the appropriate time and execute the branch instruction... To continue the loading process after the desired portion of the program has been executed, the programmer must provide re-entry to the load routine. (The IBM standard re-entry point is 00281.)' The LOAD control card merely 'signal[s] the processor that a load program should precede the object deck.' Neither passage mentions clearing core or word marks.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1, p.19 (EX) and p.17 (LOAD control card) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: MISSED, and it bounds what a card load can overwrite: the 1410 Read a Card operation 'is stopped by the first group-mark-word-mark sensed in core storage', and 'A group-mark-word-mark must appear in the core-storage position to the immediate right of the data record.' So the extent a load-mode read touches is set by a GMWM already resident in core, not by the card's own length -- another reason the pre-load state of core is load-bearing for a warm start.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3, p.62 (Read a Card) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf

additions.claim: Constant/literal size limits, useful for assembler validation and absent from the finding. C28-0309-1 p.8: 'A literal can be up to 52 characters in length, including the sign; i.e., it must be contained in one line of the coding sheet, and it must not extend beyond column 72.' C28-0326-2 p.28: 'The first blank column encountered in the operand field terminates a numeric constant. A numeric constant cannot be more than 51 characters long if it is signed; 52 if unsigned.' C28-0309-1 p.8 also gives the alphamerical terminator scan: 'the processor proceeds to column 72 of the card and searches right to left for the terminal @ symbol.'
additions.source: IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1 p.8; IBM 1410/7010 OS Autocoder C28-0326-2 p.28 - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0309-1_1410_autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: Nuance on unsigned DCW constants that partly conflicts with the finding's fact #28 framing. Fact #28 cites the LITERAL rule ('To store an unsigned number, use an alphamerical literal', C28-0309-1 p.8) alongside the DCW sign rule. For a DCW constant the OS Autocoder is explicit that unsigned is allowed and stays unsigned: 'Unsigned constants will be unsigned in storage.' The 'use an alphamerical literal' restriction applies to numerical LITERALS (which must be signed), not to DCW numerical constants.
additions.source: IBM 1410/7010 OS Autocoder C28-0326-2, p.28 (numeric constants in dcw) vs IBM 1410 Autocoder C28-0309-1, p.8 (numerical literals) - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/C28-0326-2_1410_OS_Autocoder.pdf

additions.claim: Observation from the reference emulator that an implementer should be aware of but which I could NOT match to manual text: SIMH i7010_chan.c forces a word mark onto the first character of an input record in MOVE mode -- `if (dcmd & 0200) cmd[chan] |= CHAN_LOAD; else cmd[chan] |= CHAN_WM; /* Force first char to have word mark set */`. A22-0526-3 p.41 says only that in move mode 'Word separators in incoming data are stored unchanged as word separators in core storage', with no mention of a word mark being set at the leftmost position. This is either an undocumented hardware behaviour or a SIMH quirk; I could not resolve which from the manuals I read.
additions.source: SIMH I7000 simulator i7010_chan.c ~line 468 - https://github.com/open-simh/simh/blob/master/I7000/i7010_chan.c ; cf. IBM 1410 Principles of Operation A22-0526-3 p.41 - https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf

notes:
METHOD. All three primary manuals were already cached locally in this session's scratchpad as OCR text extracts (C28-0309-1, C28-0326-2, A22-0526-3, plus the IBM 1401 A24-1403-5 reference and SIMH's i7010_chan.c). I verified against those text extracts and, for the one place OCR had scrambled a figure's row order, read a single PDF page image (C28-0309-1 PDF page 7 = printed page 7, Figure 2). PDF page number equals printed page number in the bitsavers scan of C28-0309-1 -- I confirmed this by checking page 9 independently -- so the finding's page citations for that manual are trustworthy.

RE-CONFIRMED VERBATIM (no change needed; not listed under 'upgraded' because they were already tagged verified): the C28-0309-1 p.12 DCW rule; the C28-0326-2 p.28 DCW restatement and column-7 indent rule; the C28-0326-2 p.30 DS sentence, word for word; the C28-0309-1 p.13 DC and DS sentences; the C28-0326-2 p.30 DS label rule; the C28-0309-1 p.13 blank-constant and ,G group-mark rules; the C28-0309-1 p.14 DA field/subfield word-mark rule and the p.14 'Result: At object program load time' list; the C28-0326-2 p.25 DA no-clear ',N' option including 'not effective when the program is loaded from the sof'; all four literal claims (pooling once per program section, area-defining literal blanks via a processor-generated DCW, address-constant literal unsigned in core, address adjustment modifying the literal's address); the C28-0309-1 pp.18-19 LTORG/EX text; the C28-0326-2 p.18 'buffertwo refers to location 00596 (the low-order position of the field)'; the A22-0526-3 p.7 word-mark rules; the A22-0526-3 p.62 Read a Card 'If the L Op code is used, word separators are read into storage as word marks'; the word-separator-as-first-character restriction and its non-application to DC.

APPENDIX C LISTING SPOT-CHECK. I checked every row of the finding's Exhibit IV table against the OCR of C28-0326-2 pp.56-57. All of it holds: BXPA 7/00192, DCW #5 5/00203, DCW AREA 5/00208 value 00315, PCH B 7/00209, EOF EQU * 00216, LTORG * 00302, IDENT#5 5/00306, 3-char literal 00309, 1-char literal 00310, CNT#4 4/00314, AREA DA 1X80 81/00315 with a blank CARD column, AR04 00318, AR80 00394, indented EOJ DC 6/00396 and ERR DC 6/00402, MLCB AR80,IDENT#5 assembling to D 00394 00306 L. The finding's arithmetic chains are all correct.

THE 1401-CONFUSION HUNT (the thing I was asked to hunt hardest for) turned up exactly one instance, and it runs the opposite way from what the finding asserts: the finding invents a 1401-vs-1410 divergence in card load-mode word-mark handling that does not exist. See refutation 1. Everything else in the findings is 1410-specific and correctly attributed -- the DCW/DC/DS/DA semantics are quoted from 1410 Autocoder manuals, not back-filled from 1401 Autocoder practice, which was my main worry going in.

WHAT I COULD NOT SETTLE. (a) Whether real 1410 hardware clears pre-existing word marks in load mode. The manuals are silent; SIMH says it clears; the 1401's analogous storage-to-storage Load instruction also clears ('A load instruction moves the word mark and data from the A-field to the B-field, and clears any other word marks in the designated B-field, up to the length of the A-field', A24-1403-5). The weight of evidence favours clearing, but no primary 1410 source states it, so I have flagged the finding's confidence rather than asserting the opposite as verified. This is the single highest-value remaining unknown for the emulator and would be worth resolving against the 1411 CE manual (223-2692, also cached) or ILD logic before committing to a model. (b) The finding's other four open questions all stand as genuinely open -- I found nothing in C28-0309-1 or C28-0326-2 on DA punch encoding, on multi-card constant splitting, or on whether the tape Autocoder's DA cleared its area, and no other 1410 manual I searched (Operating Guide C28-0351-5, System Monitor C28-0319-4, OS Autocoder -1) describes the condensed card format at all.
